claim: Scrub-jay caching of food in the place where food will be missing (Raby 2007, N=8, one test evening after 6 training mornings) has not been reproduced by two independent labs in two other corvid species (Eurasian jays, Canada jays). Raby primary counts were not read. Gap search: still no same-species (western scrub-jay) re-run; the original lab no longer houses the species (Farrar 2020). Raby counts still not read.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent; background only.

claim: Eurasian jays (Amodio 2021, pre-registered) fit a compartment-independent caching model best (posterior 0.997 in Exp 1; 0.72 in Exp 2), far above Future Planning (0.0014; 0.002). Only one bird (Lisbon) cached as Future Planning predicts.
agent_test: Fit the same Bayesian model set to an agent's choices to see if it tracks future need or just spreads caches.

claim: Canada jays (Martin 2021, N=6) cached more in the feeding compartment, the opposite of Raby (F(1,15)=12.18, p<0.001); 3 of 6 did not cache in the breakfast-choice experiment.
agent_test: None.

claim: Cheke and Clayton 2012 (N=4 Eurasian jays) found future-need caching after a specific satiety check, but N is tiny and Amodio 2021 did not reproduce it with a Raby-style design.
agent_test: None.

claim: Early positive jay results (Correia 2007) are cited second-hand here; exact cache counts for Raby 2007 and Correia 2007 were never read in the primary text. Gap search 2026-11-19: Raby is paywalled (abstract and figure captions only) and Correia was blocked for automated download; counts remain unread.
agent_test: Retrieve the primary tables before using any jay effect size.

claim: Future-oriented tool choice is reported in apes and ravens (Mulcahy and Call 2006: 7/16 average; Kabadayi and Osvath 2017: delays up to 17 h) but counts and N were not read in primary text, and Suddendorf and Corballis dispute the apes.
agent_test: None.

claim: New Caledonian crows pass a pre-registered spoon test: 4 of 6 trained crows reached criterion; three of four scored 9/10, 7/10, 7/10 (chance 20%), one 3/10. Critics say prior training may explain results. Gap search: no second lab or extra crows have been reported; the 2021 reply by the authors adds argument but no data.
agent_test: Spoon-style test: show an apparatus, remove it, offer five tools after a delay; compare agent with and without scratch notes at equal tokens.

claim: Children under five fail multi-step foresight tasks that are easy in the instant form: instant 91.7% correct, delayed 50% (chance 16.7%; F(1,22)=12.79).
agent_test: None.

claim: Episodic-like memory in scrub-jays did not replicate cleanly: in Davies 2025 only 4 jays did both delays, cached-vs-control W=4, p=0.068 (lowest possible p with that N), long-delay first-search pattern unclear.
agent_test: Compare what-where-when recall from an agent memory store at short vs long delay with one item type decaying.

claim: Humans plan flexibly across needs and contexts; the key animal test (Bischof-Kohler hypothesis) was framed by Suddendorf and Corballis; animals pass only narrow cases so far.
agent_test: None; background framing.

Positive imagery g=0.64, neutral or negative about 0. Gap search: both abstracts re-read via Europe PMC and match; full texts still unread (abstract-level).
agent_test: Prompt the agent to imagine a vivid positive future outcome before a patient-vs-impulsive choice; compare choice rates at equal tokens.

claim: AI-generated future selves change human decisions: Poonsiriwong 2025 (N=192) two-sided avatar switch rate 34.2% vs 10.8% control (p=0.015); novel option chosen 20.0% vs 2.7% (p=0.019).
agent_test: None; human-facing.

claim: Future You (Pataranutaporn 2024, N=344): anxiety change -0.68 vs +0.21 control, future self-continuity +0.42 vs 0.00. A 2025 follow-up (N=92) found no format differences.
agent_test: None; human-facing.

claim: LLMs show prospective-memory failure under load: formatting-constraint compliance drops 2-21% under concurrent task load (mean drops: o4-mini 8.9, DeepSeek-V3.1 10.2, Llama-3.3-70B 6.0 points); terminal constraints drop up to 50%.
agent_test: Add a trailing constraint reminder to the final step; measure compliance at equal tokens.

claim: A salience-enhanced format (explicit framing plus trailing reminder) restores LLM compliance to 90-100% in many cells (5xGSM8K: DeepSeek 100% vs 72.2%, Llama 98.1% vs 70.4%). Cost found in the same paper: with constraint plus reminder, o4-mini GSM8K x3 accuracy is 26.7% vs 93.3% single-task (DeepSeek 76.7, Llama 64.4).
agent_test: Add a final constraint-check state; compare compliance at equal tokens.

claim: LLM prospective memory degrades with context length: TriggerBench PM accuracy falls from over 90% to under 40% at 100K tokens for GPT-4o while retrospective memory stays about 98%; Qwen3-235B-Think stays about 90%.
agent_test: Insert a latent trigger at 20K vs 100K tokens of filler; measure action rate.

claim: Reasoning helps LLM prospective memory but raises false alarms: GPT-5.2 gains 13.91 points from no thinking to high effort yet scores 43.94% on negative controls; Qwen3-235B-Think PM Acc 74.86%.
agent_test: Measure hit rate and false-alarm rate on matched negative controls.

claim: LLM agents reach only 65.1% Set-F1 on PM-Bench (best: GPT-5.4 with heartbeat); a todo ledger gives 62.8% with fewest false positives; typed intention stores reach 82.9% with DeepSeek-Chat and lift a 2B model from 4.2% to 66.2%. Gap search: an independent group (Pro-Memory, 2611.05731) reports PM-Bench Set-F1 0.7600 with Claude Sonnet 4.5 (no memory 0.5224) and 0.7324 with Haiku 4.5 (no memory 0.4561), plus gains on a second benchmark, ProactiveBench (F1 0.7376 Sonnet, 0.6634 Haiku). All preprints, authors' own methods.
agent_test: Add a typed intention ledger; compare Set-F1 against a plain notes buffer.

claim: Prospection-guided retrieval (imagine plausible next steps, use them as probes) raises MemoryQuest recall from 0.58 (query-only) and 0.256 (Mem0) to 0.723; tree 0.723 vs chain 0.718 shows branching adds little.
agent_test: Generate 3 imagined next steps and use each as a query; compare recall at equal retrieval tokens.

claim: Proactive agents fail mostly at root-cause identification: best end-to-end 40% (GPT-5 and Claude Opus 4.1); incorrect root cause is 73.8% of identification failures.
agent_test: Seed hidden-cause scenarios and score root-cause accuracy.

claim: Frontier LLMs match rodent reference values on text-based animal paradigms (CheeseBench v2, 15 May 2026): Claude Opus 4.7 86.7% vs rodent 78.9%; radial arm maze open-weight best 10%, Opus 4.7 100%, Opus 4.6 90%, GPT-4.1 0%; frontier runs only 10 trials per environment. Version resolved: v1 (12 Apr) reports best open-weight 52.6% vs random 32.1%; v2 reports 68.0% vs 38.0%. The arXiv abstract page still shows the v1 numbers, so use v2 full text.
agent_test: Run radial-arm-style revisit tasks with and without CoT at equal tokens.

claim: No direct LLM test of the scrub-jay caching, future-need choice or Bischof-Kohler paradigm was found after about 22 searches in total (about 10 more arXiv listing queries in the gap search). Only adjacent tests exist: prospective-memory benchmarks, CheeseBench, and a delay-of-gratification micro-benchmark.
agent_test: Build a caching analogue: agent hides items, gets different hunger states, picks locations.

claim: Foresight is not always found in the field: flying squirrels track past, not future, resource abundance (delta AIC 26-29 when future variables added).

claim: Delay of gratification in corvids depends on social context: all 6 crows chose delayed in all 3 conditions; no jay did when anyone was present. Thom and Clayton 2014 found no caching preference by future recovery time (F(1.37,15.07)=0.123, p=.808).
agent_test: None.

claim: Planning scaffolds (generative agents, self-regulated simulative planning) are reported useful but are not controlled prospection tests: the planning ablation was abstract-only; the 25.8-95.3% token saving comes from an RL-trained model.
agent_test: Ablate a prospective-simulation step at equal tokens.

claim: No large-N or pre-registered western scrub-jay replication of Raby 2007 was found. The structural reason given by the original lab is that it no longer houses California scrub-jays; the only same-design re-run is in Canada jays (N=6, opposite direction). Amodio 2021 lists design differences (housing, trial length 2 h vs 15 min, stable vs rotating place-condition link).
agent_test: None; background only.

claim: Retrospective memory can lower proactive-agent accuracy: on Claude Haiku 4.5, ProactiveBench F1 is 0.5103 with no memory but 0.3636 with RAG, 0.3276 with A-Mem and 0.3248 with T-Mem; Pro-Memory reaches 0.6634. Removing intention-evidence links on Haiku lowers PM-Bench Set-F1 by 8.45 points and more than doubles false alarms. Token cost of Pro-Memory is 1.61M (Sonnet) and 1.10M (Haiku) per full run, below RWM at 1.28x and 1.91x.
agent_test: Compare plain retrieval against a pending-intention ledger on the same agent task at equal tokens.

claim: The reminder that restores prospective-memory compliance can cost main-task accuracy: o4-mini GSM8K x3 falls from 93.3% (single, no constraint) to 26.7% with constraint plus reminder; DeepSeek 76.7%, Llama 64.4%. Tested on three models only, max 2048 tokens.
agent_test: Measure task accuracy and constraint compliance together when adding a trailing reminder.

claim: Strong reasoning models keep prospective memory better but degrade with context and false-alarm: TriggerBench PM Acc at 40K context GPT-5.2 (high) 75.02 with negative-clean 39.80; Qwen3-235B-Think 52.65; GPT-4.1 45.22. Column labels were inferred from flattened text.
agent_test: Report hit rate and false-alarm rate together when testing reminders.

claim: The only LLM test close to a delay-of-gratification paradigm is a persona-driven ReAct micro-benchmark (19,200 trajectories; 75.9% persist; removing hedonic drive and age persona raises completion toward 1.0). It tests waiting under prompts, not choosing for a different future state.
agent_test: Not a prospection test; a caching analogue is still needed.

claim: LLM-written episodic-future-thinking cues have only feasibility evidence (EFTeacher, GPT-4-Turbo: usability and interviews, no discounting outcome); the human meta-analytic effect (g 0.44, 0.52) has not been tested on an LLM agent's own choices.
agent_test: Test a vivid, concrete future-outcome prompt on an agent patient-vs-impulsive choice at equal tokens.
